implementation_notes: Scala's poltergeist is either a case class wrapper whose only method delegates, or a case object whose single method calls a collaborator obtained by injection. The idiomatic replacements are a companion-object method (where Scala already puts constructors and derived operations) and a function in the companion of the type that owns the data. An `implicit` that resolves to a helper object is the Scala-specific hazard: it makes the helper live without any reference a reader can follow, and it is indistinguishable from a legitimate typeclass instance.
idiom_name: case class with one method delegating to another type
pitfalls: An implicit val of a helper type is a poltergeist that no grep will find, because the reference is resolved rather than written.
`case object` helpers holding mutable state are the singleton version of the smell.
A case class with a single field used only for pattern matching is an ADT variant, not a poltergeist.
